messages:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 tail latency spike detected on cont-batching path for streaming route /v1/stream. p99 > 3s, paging eng-oncall. Auto-snooze in 5m unless acked.

Alice Chen: acked — I'm on it. quick snapshot: p95 ~ 900ms, p99 ~ 3.6s, streaming stall rate +1.2% (sessions with >2s stalls). No increase in 5xxs.

Raj Patel: jumping in — I see queue depth spike on cont-batch scheduler (node-gpu-14 group). Metrics: enqueue_count up x3, avg_batch_tokens jumped from ~190 -> ~560. Mixed sequence length mix looks bad.

Samir K.: digging through runtime logs. Observed KV cache churn and a bunch of long-seq sessions that never hit prefix cache. CPU on the host spiked which delayed scheduling. paste logs:

```
[cont-batch] ts=2026-03-14T09:12:01Z enqueue_size=128->1024
[sched] node=node-gpu-14 preempt_count=24 fair_share=0.12
[latency] p95=920ms p99=3620ms streaming_stalls=1.2%\n```

Maya Lopez: hypothesis: continuous batching is accumulating very long sequences into large batches, which elongates service time for the whole batch (tail amplification). Two short-term knobs: limit max batch tokens or enable per-seqlen lane separation.

Alice Chen: can we apply a soft mitigation now? I can patch routing to cap max_batch_tokens and enable soft preemption for long jobs. That should reduce worst-case batch sizes quickly.

Raj Patel: +1. Also add an admission control threshold so super-long requests bypass cont-batch and go to low-throughput dedicated workers. That avoids blocking streaming latency.

Maya Lopez: proposed immediate commands:
```
# cap batch tokens to 256 for streaming pool
curl -XPOST https://ops.redwood.internal/api/v1/config \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"service":"cont-batch","pool":"streaming","max_batch_tokens":256}'\n
# soft preemption on
curl -XPOST https://ops.redwood.internal/api/v1/config \
  -d '{"service":"cont-batch","preempt_mode":"soft"}'
```

Deploy Bot: applying change to cont-batch pool: set max_batch_tokens=256, preempt_mode=soft. Rolling restart on 12 nodes, expected ramp 90s.

Alice Chen: patch applied. watching.

(2m) Alice Chen: initial improvement visible: p99 dropped from 3.6s -> 1.4s, p95 ~ 430ms. streaming stalls down to 0.45%.

Samir K.: note: fairness got a little worse for tiny requests — some short sessions saw higher latency because scheduler now has more small windows between preemptions. Need to tune fair-share weights and per-seqlen lanes as next step.

Kevin (Support): any customer-impact notes? I saw one high-volume customer (acct: acme-inc) report intermittent stalls in the last 30m. Should we notify them that mitigation is in place?

Alice Chen: yes, please ping Acme with an interim note: we identified cont-batch tail latencies caused by mixed long sequences; applied temp mitigation (capped batch tokens + soft preempt). We're monitoring; follow-up with permanent fix ETA.

Raj Patel: long-term plan (action items):
- add seqlen-based lanes in scheduler (short/medium/long) to avoid head-of-line blocking
- implement admission-control to route >X tokens to dedicated pool
- update fairshare algorithm to consider recent preemptions
- add per-customer seqlen heatmap to alerting

Maya Lopez: created a repro locally with a synthetic mix (10% long sequences >800 tokens). Verified that with lanes, p99 stabilizes <700ms. Will open PR for scheduler lanes.

Samir K.: creating incident ticket: INF-2026-314. I'll attach perf graphs, logs, and the mitigation command history.

Deploy Bot: incident label applied: severity=high, owner=eng-oncall, linked: INF-2026-314.

Alice Chen: I'm staying on for next 30m to observe. After that I'll hand off to Raj. Handoff note: mitigation applied (max_batch_tokens=256, preempt_mode=soft), immediate metrics improved but fairness tradeoff exists. Long-term fixes queued.

Raj Patel: I'll take the 23:00 PST handoff. My TODOs during handoff: validate lane PR on canary, roll out admission-control to 5% traffic, and coordinate CS message.

Kevin (Support): I'll draft the customer message and post it to the Acme thread.

Incident Bot: reminder: autogenerate postmortem template and assign to Samir. Next update in 20m or on next significant metric change. :thumbsup:

Alice Chen: quick summary for handoff -> 23:00 PST:
- Impact: p99 spike to ~3.6s, p95 ~900ms, streaming stalls +1.2% for ~45m, one customer (Acme) reported degraded UX
- Cause: cont-batch tail amplification due to mixed seq lengths + scheduler fairness edge-case + KV cache churn
- Short-term mitigation: set max_batch_tokens=256 & preempt_mode=soft (applied) -> p99 -> ~1.1s
- Next steps: scheduler lanes PR (Maya), admission-control rollout (Raj), fairshare tuning (Samir), customer comms (Kevin)

Samir K.: handing incident to Raj on-call. I'll keep INF-2026-314 updated with logs and attachments.

Raj Patel: taking handoff. If anything regresses ping me @raj. Let's keep incident open until scheduler lanes are canaried.

Deploy Bot: thread closed for now; reopening on metric regression or manual re-open.
